name: Agent Activity Tracker

# Reconciles which issues/PRs currently have at least one factory workflow
# in progress. Applies the `agent-working` label and a `model:<name>` label
# derived from the workflow's engine.model so the Projects board can show
# "something is actively chewing on this."
#
# Trade-off: the tracker polls every 5 minutes instead of being event-driven,
# because workflow_run only fires on completion (not on queued) and still
# requires an API round-trip to find the triggering item. Polling keeps the
# sync rule simple and idempotent.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/5 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: read

concurrency:
  group: agent-activity-tracker
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  reconcile:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          sparse-checkout: .github/workflows
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Reconcile agent-working labels
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # Factory workflows we care about. Anything else (CI, etc.) is not
          # an "agent" in the factory sense and we ignore it.
          FACTORY_WORKFLOWS=(
            "Agentic Triage"
            "Spec Refiner"
            "Implementer Dispatcher"
            "Reviewer"
            "Contribution Checker"
            "Simplify & Harden CI"
            "Eval Creator CI"
            "PR Fix"
            "Conflict Resolver"
            "Self-Improvement Meta"
            "Learning Aggregator CI"
            "CI Cleaner"
          )

          # Build a jq filter matching any of the factory workflow names.
          WF_FILTER=$(printf '"%s",' "${FACTORY_WORKFLOWS[@]}")
          WF_FILTER="[${WF_FILTER%,}]"

          echo "::group::Fetching in-progress factory runs"
          RUNS=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs?status=in_progress&per_page=50" \
            --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name as \$n | $WF_FILTER | index(\$n))] | map({id: .id, name: .name, path: .path, event: .event})")
          echo "$RUNS" | jq '.'
          echo "::endgroup::"

          declare -A ACTIVE_ITEMS    # item_num -> 1
          declare -A ACTIVE_MODELS   # item_num -> "gpt-5.4 claude-sonnet-4-6"

          for row in $(echo "$RUNS" | jq -r '.[] | @base64'); do
            RUN=$(echo "$row" | base64 -d)
            RUN_ID=$(echo "$RUN" | jq -r '.id')
            WF_PATH=$(echo "$RUN" | jq -r '.path')

            # Look up the engine.model from the workflow's .md source.
            # Compiled .lock.yml has no human-readable model; read the .md.
            MD_PATH="${WF_PATH%.lock.yml}.md"
            if [ -f "$MD_PATH" ]; then
              MODEL=$(awk '/^engine:/{inside=1; next} inside && /^[^ ]/{inside=0} inside && /model:/ {print $2; exit}' "$MD_PATH" | tr -d '"')
            else
              MODEL=""
            fi

            # Extract triggering issue/PR number from the run's event payload.
            ITEM_NUM=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID" \
              --jq '.. | .number? | numbers' | head -1)
            if [ -z "$ITEM_NUM" ]; then
              continue
            fi

            ACTIVE_ITEMS[$ITEM_NUM]=1
            if [ -n "$MODEL" ]; then
              ACTIVE_MODELS[$ITEM_NUM]="${ACTIVE_MODELS[$ITEM_NUM]:-} $MODEL"
            fi
          done

          echo "Active items: ${!ACTIVE_ITEMS[@]}"

          # Apply labels on currently-active items.
          for num in "${!ACTIVE_ITEMS[@]}"; do
            gh issue edit "$num" --add-label agent-working 2>/dev/null || \
              gh pr edit "$num" --add-label agent-working 2>/dev/null || true

            # Unique-sort the model list for this item.
            MODELS=$(echo "${ACTIVE_MODELS[$num]:-}" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -v '^$' | sort -u)
            for m in $MODELS; do
              LBL="model:$m"
              # Ensure the label exists (idempotent create, ignore if already present).
              gh label create "$LBL" --color D4C5F9 --description "Active gh-aw workflow engine.model" 2>/dev/null || true
              gh issue edit "$num" --add-label "$LBL" 2>/dev/null || \
                gh pr edit "$num" --add-label "$LBL" 2>/dev/null || true
            done
          done

          # Sweep: remove agent-working + model:* from items no longer active.
          LABELED=$(gh issue list --label agent-working --state all --json number --jq '.[].number')
          LABELED_PRS=$(gh pr list --label agent-working --state all --json number --jq '.[].number')
          for num in $LABELED $LABELED_PRS; do
            if [ -z "${ACTIVE_ITEMS[$num]:-}" ]; then
              gh issue edit "$num" --remove-label agent-working 2>/dev/null || \
                gh pr edit "$num" --remove-label agent-working 2>/dev/null || true
              # Remove any model:* label on this item.
              EXISTING=$(gh issue view "$num" --json labels --jq '.labels[].name' 2>/dev/null || \
                gh pr view "$num" --json labels --jq '.labels[].name' 2>/dev/null || true)
              for lbl in $EXISTING; do
                case "$lbl" in
                  model:*)
                    gh issue edit "$num" --remove-label "$lbl" 2>/dev/null || \
                      gh pr edit "$num" --remove-label "$lbl" 2>/dev/null || true
                    ;;
                esac
              done
            fi
          done

## Summary

The tracker merged in #165 applied zero labels on its first run. Root cause: `gh api .../runs/ID --jq '.. | .number? | numbers' | head -1` returned the run's own number first, not the triggering PR number.

## Fix

Switch to `.pull_requests[0].number` and only attempt detection for `pull_request` / `pull_request_target` events. 1	name: Agent Activity Tracker
2	
3	# Reconciles which issues/PRs currently have at least one factory workflow
4	# in progress. Applies the `agent-working` label and a `model:<name>` label
5	# derived from the workflow's engine.model so the Projects board can show
6	# "something is actively chewing on this."
7	#
8	# Trade-off: the tracker polls every 5 minutes instead of being event-driven,
9	# because workflow_run only fires on completion (not on queued) and still
10	# requires an API round-trip to find the triggering item. Polling keeps the
11	# sync rule simple and idempotent.
12	
13	on:
14	  schedule:
15	    - cron: '*/5 * * * *'
16	  workflow_dispatch:
17	
18	permissions:
19	  contents: read
20	  issues: write
21	  pull-requests: write
22	  actions: read
23	
24	concurrency:
25	  group: agent-activity-tracker
26	  cancel-in-progress: true
27	
28	jobs:
29	  reconcile:
30	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
31	    steps:
32	      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
33	        with:
34	          sparse-checkout: .github/workflows
35	          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false
36	
37	      - name: Reconcile agent-working labels
38	        env:
39	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
40	          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
41	        run: |
42	          set -euo pipefail
43	
44	          # Factory workflows we care about. Anything else (CI, etc.) is not
45	          # an "agent" in the factory sense and we ignore it.
46	          FACTORY_WORKFLOWS=(
47	            "Agentic Triage"
48	            "Spec Refiner"
49	            "Implementer Dispatcher"
50	            "Reviewer"
51	            "Contribution Checker"
52	            "Simplify & Harden CI"
53	            "Eval Creator CI"
54	            "PR Fix"
55	            "Conflict Resolver"
56	            "Self-Improvement Meta"
57	            "Learning Aggregator CI"
58	            "CI Cleaner"
59	          )
60	
61	          # Build a jq filter matching any of the factory workflow names.
62	          WF_FILTER=$(printf '"%s",' "${FACTORY_WORKFLOWS[@]}")
63	          WF_FILTER="[${WF_FILTER%,}]"
64	
65	          echo "::group::Fetching in-progress factory runs"
66	          RUNS=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs?status=in_progress&per_page=50" \
67	            --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name as \$n | $WF_FILTER | index(\$n))] | map({id: .id, name: .name, path: .path, event: .event})")
68	          echo "$RUNS" | jq '.'
69	          echo "::endgroup::"
70	
71	          declare -A ACTIVE_ITEMS    # item_num -> 1
72	          declare -A ACTIVE_MODELS   # item_num -> "gpt-5.4 claude-sonnet-4-6"
73	
74	          for row in $(echo "$RUNS" | jq -r '.[] | @base64'); do
75	            RUN=$(echo "$row" | base64 -d)
76	            RUN_ID=$(echo "$RUN" | jq -r '.id')
77	            WF_PATH=$(echo "$RUN" | jq -r '.path')
78	
79	            # Look up the engine.model from the workflow's .md source.
80	            # Compiled .lock.yml has no human-readable model; read the .md.
81	            MD_PATH="${WF_PATH%.lock.yml}.md"
82	            if [ -f "$MD_PATH" ]; then
83	              MODEL=$(awk '/^engine:/{inside=1; next} inside && /^[^ ]/{inside=0} inside && /model:/ {print $2; exit}' "$MD_PATH" | tr -d '"')
84	            else
85	              MODEL=""
86	            fi
87	
88	            # Extract triggering issue/PR number from the run's event payload.
89	            ITEM_NUM=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID" \
90	              --jq '.. | .number? | numbers' | head -1)
91	            if [ -z "$ITEM_NUM" ]; then
92	              continue
93	            fi
94	
95	            ACTIVE_ITEMS[$ITEM_NUM]=1
96	            if [ -n "$MODEL" ]; then
97	              ACTIVE_MODELS[$ITEM_NUM]="${ACTIVE_MODELS[$ITEM_NUM]:-} $MODEL"
98	            fi
99	          done
100	
101	          echo "Active items: ${!ACTIVE_ITEMS[@]}"
102	
103	          # Apply labels on currently-active items.
104	          for num in "${!ACTIVE_ITEMS[@]}"; do
105	            gh issue edit "$num" --add-label agent-working 2>/dev/null || \
106	              gh pr edit "$num" --add-label agent-working 2>/dev/null || true
107	
108	            # Unique-sort the model list for this item.
109	            MODELS=$(echo "${ACTIVE_MODELS[$num]:-}" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -v '^$' | sort -u)
110	            for m in $MODELS; do
111	              LBL="model:$m"
112	              # Ensure the label exists (idempotent create, ignore if already present).
113	              gh label create "$LBL" --color D4C5F9 --description "Active gh-aw workflow engine.model" 2>/dev/null || true
114	              gh issue edit "$num" --add-label "$LBL" 2>/dev/null || \
115	                gh pr edit "$num" --add-label "$LBL" 2>/dev/null || true
116	            done
117	          done
118	
119	          # Sweep: remove agent-working + model:* from items no longer active.
120	          LABELED=$(gh issue list --label agent-working --state all --json number --jq '.[].number')
121	          LABELED_PRS=$(gh pr list --label agent-working --state all --json number --jq '.[].number')
122	          for num in $LABELED $LABELED_PRS; do
123	            if [ -z "${ACTIVE_ITEMS[$num]:-}" ]; then
124	              gh issue edit "$num" --remove-label agent-working 2>/dev/null || \
125	                gh pr edit "$num" --remove-label agent-working 2>/dev/null || true
126	              # Remove any model:* label on this item.
127	              EXISTING=$(gh issue view "$num" --json labels --jq '.labels[].name' 2>/dev/null || \
128	                gh pr view "$num" --json labels --jq '.labels[].name' 2>/dev/null || true)
129	              for lbl in $EXISTING; do
130	                case "$lbl" in
131	                  model:*)
132	                    gh issue edit "$num" --remove-label "$lbl" 2>/dev/null || \
133	                      gh pr edit "$num" --remove-label "$lbl" 2>/dev/null || true
134	                    ;;
135	                esac
136	              done
137	            fi
138	          done

`self-improvement-meta` runs every night around 2am. It:

1. Reads the last 24 hours of workflow run logs
2. Extracts failure patterns and categorizes them (prompt, tool, context, data)
3. Deduplicates against existing entries in `.learnings/LEARNINGS.md`
4. Opens a PR that adds prevention rules to `AGENTS.md` or the relevant workflow file

When you merge that PR, the next run of the affected agent reads the updated instructions. The factory gets smarter every day. If there are no failures, it calls noop. Silence is the correct signal when the factory is healthy.

## Controlling the Chain

| Action | How |
|--------|-----|
| **Pause any step** | Add the `human-review` label. All agents check for it and call noop. |
| **Skip spec-refinement** | Label the issue `needs-plan` directly instead of `needs-spec` |
| **Skip automated review** | Label the PR `human-review` and review it yourself |
| **Trigger manually** | Every workflow has `workflow_dispatch` enabled. Run from the Actions tab. |
| **Fix a failing PR** | Comment `/pr-fix` on the PR |
| **Fast-forward simple changes** | For trivial fixes, skip the whole chain: just open a PR directly |

## All Workflows

## Landing a PR that modifies a protected workflow file

The reviewer's [self-tamper guard](../.github/workflows/reviewer.md) applies the `human-review` label and noops before running any checks if the PR diff touches any of these paths:

- `.github/workflows/reviewer.md`
- `.github/workflows/self-improvement-meta.md`
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`

This is intentional: these files can alter the reviewer's own instructions or adjacent guardrails, so a model review of them is not a meaningful signal. Human eyes are required.

### What happens automatically

1. Reviewer applies `human-review` and calls noop.
2. `contribution-checker`, `simplify-and-harden-ci`, and `eval-creator-ci` also noop — they respect the `human-review` label as an emergency stop.
3. CI (tests, lockfile sync) still runs normally and must pass.

### How to unblock the PR

1. Read the diff yourself. Pay attention to whether it weakens guards, changes the self-tamper list, or alters review logic.
2. If the change is correct and intentional, **remove the `human-review` label** from the PR. The quality-gate workflows will NOT rerun on label removal by design — you are now the reviewer of record.
3. Merge the PR.

If the change needs work, leave `human-review` on and either push fixes to the branch yourself or ask the PR author to.

### When the guard fires on an unrelated PR

Sometimes a PR touches a protected file as a side effect of an otherwise routine change (e.g. a lockfile regeneration after a frontmatter tweak). Two options:

- Split the PR. Land the non-protected changes through the normal factory chain, then land the protected file change as a separate PR with your own review.
- Or review the whole PR yourself using the procedure above.

Do not disable the guard to let the PR through. The guard is one line of `case` logic in [`reviewer.md`](../.github/workflows/reviewer.md) — disabling it for convenience defeats the purpose.

## All Workflows

+The reviewer's [self-tamper guard](../.github/workflows/reviewer.md) applies the `human-review` label and noops before running any checks if the PR diff touches any of these paths:
+This is intentional: these files can alter the reviewer's own instructions or adjacent guardrails, so a model review of them is not a meaningful signal. Human eyes are required.
+2. `contribution-checker`, `simplify-and-harden-ci`, and `eval-creator-ci` also noop — they respect the `human-review` label as an emergency stop.
+3. CI (tests, lockfile sync) still runs normally and must pass.
+1. Read the diff yourself. Pay attention to whether it weakens guards, changes the self-tamper list, or alters review logic.

+2. If the change is correct and intentional, **remove the `human-review` label** from the PR. The quality-gate workflows will NOT rerun on label removal by design — you are now the reviewer of record.
+If the change needs work, leave `human-review` on and either push fixes to the branch yourself or ask the PR author to.
+### When the guard fires on an unrelated PR
+Sometimes a PR touches a protected file as a side effect of an otherwise routine change (e.g. a lockfile regeneration after a frontmatter tweak). Two options:
+- Split the PR. Land the non-protected changes through the normal factory chain, then land the protected file change as a separate PR with your own review.
+- Or review the whole PR yourself using the procedure above.
+Do not disable the guard to let the PR through. The guard is one line of `case` logic in [`reviewer.md`](../.github/workflows/reviewer.md) — disabling it for convenience defeats the purpose.

input.content:
## Problem

`spec-refiner` has a valid "not plan-worthy" skip path (docs change, trivial fix, pure research). When it fires, spec-refiner calls `noop` with an explanatory comment. But the issue then sits stuck with the `needs-spec` label and no automated transition forward — no plan PR to merge, no implementer assignment, no path to a fix.

This has happened twice in recent runs:

- **#153** — spec-refiner noop'd, issue sat idle until a human rewrote it as a plan PR manually.
- **#162** — same pattern. Noop message said "fastest path is a direct PR," but no direct PR was produced. Resolved by a human writing the direct PR outside the factory.

The factory's claim is "one issue, one automated pipeline, human merges." When the pipeline drops the issue, the claim breaks. A new operator seeing a `needs-spec` issue doesn't know whether the factory is still working on it, failed, or deliberately kicked it back.

## Goal

Close the loop: when spec-refiner decides an issue doesn't need a plan, the issue must transition to a state where *something else* drives it forward — either an automated implementer assignment or a clearly-labeled "human action required" state.

## Possible directions (not prescriptive — plan-refiner should pick)

1. **Route directly to implementer**. When spec-refiner judges an issue as simple-enough-for-direct-PR, it removes `needs-spec`, adds `ready-for-implementation` and `impl:copilot`, and `implementer-dispatcher` picks it up. Copilot writes the direct PR. No plan file.

2. **Explicit "no plan needed" state**. Spec-refiner swaps `needs-spec` for a new label like `no-plan-needed`. Board shows this as "human writes direct PR" column. Human is signaled to pick up manually.

3. **Plan file with empty implementation section**. Spec-refiner still writes a plan file, but the plan itself is one line ("direct PR, see issue body"). The plan PR cascades normally through `plan-merged-dispatcher` -> `ready-for-implementation`. Consistent with the rest of the chain at the cost of one tiny plan file per trivial change.

## Success criteria

- After merge, an issue labeled `needs-spec` either gets a plan PR, gets auto-routed to an implementer, or lands in a state a board view can clearly filter for "needs human."
- Zero issues end up in the `needs-spec` limbo state for >1 workflow cycle.
- #153 and #162 would have been resolved by the factory itself (modulo a human merge gate).

## Touch surface

- `.github/workflows/spec-refiner.md` — the noop logic.
- Possibly `.github/workflows/implementer-dispatcher.md` if direction 1 is chosen (no changes expected — already fires on `ready-for-implementation`).
- `docs/AGENT_FACTORY.md` — update the chain narrative to match whichever direction is chosen.

## Non-goals

- Do not remove the noop capability entirely. Some issues (spam, duplicates, genuinely-dropped) should be no-op'd and closed with a comment.
- Do not make spec-refiner write plan files for trivial docs changes as its default — only as option 3 if that's the chosen direction.

## 2026-04-17 — spec-refiner wrote `Fixes #NN` in plan PR body

**Area**: infra (factory) · **Status**: in_progress · **Tracked in**: new follow-up issue

**What happened**

Plan PR #164 (generated by spec-refiner for source issue #161) included these lines in its body:

```
Refs #161
...
- Fixes #161
```

When the plan PR merged, GitHub's auto-close-linked-issue behavior triggered on `Fixes #161` and closed the source issue #161. The source issue was supposed to stay open so `implementer-dispatcher` could assign Copilot to produce the impl PR. Instead #161 closed prematurely and the B1 state-machine-doc work stalled until a human reopened it and re-toggled `ready-for-implementation`.

**Root cause**

`.github/workflows/spec-refiner.md` has explicit instructions:

> Body references the source issue with `Refs #NN` (not a closing keyword such as `Closes` or `Fixes`). The plan PR must not close the source issue on merge.

The model followed the `Refs` part but still included `Fixes #NN` elsewhere in the body (likely as part of a boilerplate footer template). The wording treats the rule as a positive instruction ("do X") rather than a negative prohibition ("NEVER include Closes/Fixes/Resolves").

**Prevention**

- Harden the spec-refiner instruction: call out the three forbidden keywords (`Closes`, `Fixes`, `Resolves`) by name, in a "NEVER" bullet, separate from the positive `Refs` instruction.
- Add a reviewer check (B5 territory): if a plan-backed PR body contains any of those keywords targeting the source issue, flag it.
- Optional defense-in-depth: `plan-merged-dispatcher` could detect the source issue being closed on plan-PR merge and reopen it automatically.

**Impact**

- #161 closed prematurely, then reopened by hand. B1 deliverable still in flight as of this log.
- Every plan PR merge since factory inception should be audited retrospectively for the same bug.

input.content:
## Problem

Spec-refiner's plan PR body is supposed to reference the source issue using `Refs #NN` — never `Closes`, `Fixes`, or `Resolves`. Those are GitHub closing keywords: if any appear anywhere in the plan PR body, GitHub auto-closes the source issue on plan-PR merge, breaking the handoff to `implementer-dispatcher`.

The spec-refiner workflow has an explicit instruction:

> Body references the source issue with `Refs #NN` (not a closing keyword such as `Closes` or `Fixes`). The plan PR must not close the source issue on merge.

**But it happened anyway.** On 2026-04-17, plan PR #164 (for source issue #161) included `- Fixes #161` in its body. Merging the plan PR closed #161 prematurely. Factory work for B1 stalled until a human reopened the issue.

Logged in `.learnings/ERRORS.md` (2026-04-17 entry).

## Goal

Plan PRs never close source issues on merge, with defense in depth so the next occurrence is either prevented upstream or caught and reverted automatically.

## Possible directions (plan-refiner picks)

1. **Harden spec-refiner instruction**. Rewrite the prohibition as a prominent `NEVER include Closes / Fixes / Resolves anywhere in the PR body` bullet — separate from the positive `Refs` instruction. Current prose mixes the two.

2. **Reviewer check**. Reviewer workflow adds a pre-flight check: if the PR is labeled `plan-file` and the body contains any closing keyword targeting the source issue, apply `human-review` and noop with a clear comment explaining why.

3. **Defensive plan-merged-dispatcher**. After the dispatcher applies `ready-for-implementation`, it checks whether the source issue is `CLOSED`. If it is (because GitHub auto-closed it), reopen it with a comment and flag the plan PR body in a warning comment.

4. **Audit existing plan PRs**. Retrospectively check every merged plan PR's body for the same bug, to find orphaned source issues we haven't noticed.

## Success criteria

- A future run of spec-refiner on a `needs-spec` issue cannot produce a plan PR body containing `Closes`, `Fixes`, or `Resolves` targeting the source issue number.
- If one slips through, the factory self-corrects (reopens the source issue) within one workflow cycle.

## Touch surface

- `.github/workflows/spec-refiner.md` — instruction hardening (direction 1).
- `.github/workflows/reviewer.md` — optional check (direction 2). This would trip the self-tamper guard; would need to be shipped carefully.
- `.github/workflows/plan-merged-dispatcher.yml` — reopen logic (direction 3).

## Non-goals

- Don't disable GitHub's closing-keyword behavior globally; it's correct for normal implementation PRs.
- Don't change what spec-refiner is allowed to write in the plan PR body beyond the closing-keyword fix.

## Reference

- `.learnings/ERRORS.md` — 2026-04-17 entry with full root-cause analysis.
- Plan PR #164 — the example that triggered this.
- Source issue #161 — the one that got auto-closed.

1	# Agent Factory: End-to-End Agentic Workflows
2	
3	A complete **triage, spec, plan, implement, review, fix, learn** agent factory powered by [GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw)](https://github.github.com/gh-aw/). Workflows chain together through GitHub events (labels, PRs, comments). No orchestrator, no DAG. Each workflow does one job, hands off via a label swap, and the next workflow picks it up. This is choreography, not orchestration.
4	
5	The source issue is the unit of work end-to-end. A plan PR produces one consolidated checklist on the source issue itself; there is no sub-issue layer.
6	
7	## The Complete Chain
8	
9	```
10	issue opened
11	  |
12	  v
13	issue-triage (auto-labels by type, detects spam)
14	  |
15	  v
16	human adds "needs-spec" label
17	  |
18	  v
19	spec-refiner (plan file + implementer label on issue)
20	  |
21	  v
22	human reviews plan PR, optionally swaps implementer label  <-- ONE decision
23	  |
24	  v
25	human merges plan PR
26	  |
27	  v
28	plan-merged-dispatcher (plain Actions: writes plan checklist onto source issue body,
29	                        transitions needs-plan -> ready-for-implementation)
30	  |
31	  v
32	implementer-dispatcher (auto-assigns the source issue based on its impl:* label)
33	  |
34	  v
35	PR opened
36	  |
37	  +---> reviewer (plan-aware code review with implementer calibration)
38	  +---> contribution-checker (CONTRIBUTING.md compliance)
39	  |
40	  v
41	needs-changes? ---> /pr-fix (auto-fix CI failures)
42	  |
43	  v
44	PR labeled needs-rebase? ---> conflict-resolver (merge origin/main; push on clean merge, hand off on conflict)
45	  |
46	  v
47	CI failure on main? ---> ci-cleaner (lint, test, compile fix loop)
48	  |
49	  v
50	nightly ---> self-improvement-meta (extract learnings, commit guardrails)
51	```
52	
53	State lives in GitHub, not in memory. Each agent starts cold. Every handoff is mediated by a file, a label, or a PR. This makes the chain debuggable: you can inspect the state at any point by looking at the repo.
54	
55	## Prerequisites
56	
57	### Local tooling
58	
59	- [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) installed and authenticated (`gh auth login`)
60	- [gh-aw extension](https://github.com/github/gh-aw): `gh extension install github/gh-aw`
61	- Git 2.40+ (required by gh-aw for sparse checkouts)
62	
63	### Repository settings
64	
65	Apply these in **Settings** on the repo hosting the factory. Skipping any of these is the most common cause of the factory stalling between steps.
66	
67	| Setting | Path | Value | Why |
68	|---------|------|-------|-----|
69	| Workflow permissions | Settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions | **Read and write permissions** | Workflows need write access to push fixes, open PRs, move labels |
70	| Allow PR creation | Same page | **Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests** (checked) | `/pr-fix`, `ci-cleaner`, `self-improvement-meta` all open PRs |
71	| Outside contributor approval | Settings > Actions > General > Approval for outside collaborators | **Require approval for first-time contributors** (not "...who are new to GitHub") | The "...new to GitHub" option does NOT exempt the Copilot bot; this one does after the first merged Copilot PR |
72	| Copilot workflow approval | Settings > Copilot > Coding agent > Actions workflow approval | **Off** (recommended) or **On** (belt-and-suspenders) | Separate from the outside-contributor setting above. When **On**, every Copilot PR requires a manual "Approve and run" click before any factory workflow runs. Safe to turn off once `reviewer` + `contribution-checker` + your merge gate are in place. |
73	| Copilot Partner Agents (Claude, Codex) | Settings > Copilot > Coding agent > Partner Agents | Optional: On if you plan to hand-assign Claude/Codex via the GitHub UI | Partner Agents appear in the assignees picker when enabled, but the factory cannot auto-dispatch to them today (see "Implementer Routing" below for why). |
74	| Copilot cloud agent | Settings > Copilot > Coding agent | **Enabled** | Required for `impl:copilot` issue assignment |
75	| Copilot code review | Settings > Copilot > Code review | **Enabled for this repo** | Lets the Copilot SWE agent annotate PRs inline |
76	| Actions permissions | Settings > Actions > General > Actions permissions | **Allow all actions and reusable workflows** | Some factory workflows pull from `githubnext/agentics` and `github/gh-aw-actions` |
77	
78	### Required secrets
79	
80	Add these under **Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions**. `GITHUB_TOKEN` is provided by GitHub automatically and does not need to be created.
81	
82	| Secret | Required by | How to get it |
83	|--------|-------------|---------------|
84	| `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` | Every custom gh-aw workflow (agent runtime auth) | Personal access token with `copilot` scope, or a fine-grained token with Copilot access |
85	| `GH_AW_AGENT_TOKEN` | `implementer-dispatcher` (assigning Copilot) and `plan-merged-dispatcher` (label cascades into `implementer-dispatcher`) | PAT with `issues: write`, `contents: write`, and cascade-capable (i.e. a user/installation PAT, not `GITHUB_TOKEN`) |
86	| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | **Optional** — only if you enable `ai-proficiency-claude.yml` | Get from console.anthropic.com; skip if you stick to the Copilot-powered `ai-proficiency-pr-review` |
87	
88	You can reuse the same PAT across these if it has the union of scopes. Keep them separate if you want to rotate or revoke them independently.
89	
90	**Historical note:** earlier versions of this doc listed `GH_AW_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_AW_GITHUB_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN`, and `GH_AW_CI_TRIGGER_TOKEN` as required secrets. Those names appear in every compiled `.lock.yml` because gh-aw's default template references them, but none are actually required for this factory — gh-aw falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` when they are missing. Do **not** create them unless you have a specific need; the extra tokens just create more things to rotate.
91	
92	### Required labels
93	
94	The factory is choreographed through labels. Create these once in **Issues > Labels**. There is no automated label-setup script in this repository; create labels manually via the GitHub web UI or the `gh` CLI (for example: `gh label create needs-rebase --color e4e669 --description "PR branch needs merging with origin/main"`).
95	
96	| Label | Purpose |
97	|-------|---------|
98	| `needs-spec`, `needs-plan`, `spec-refined` | Spec refinement flow |
99	| `blocked-on-human` | Agent needs human input before proceeding |
100	| `ready-for-implementation`, `assigned-to-agent` | Implementation dispatch flow |
101	| `impl:claude-opus`, `impl:claude-sonnet`, `impl:copilot`, `impl:codex` | Implementer routing |
102	| `ai-reviewed`, `needs-changes`, `fast-track`, `spec-drift` | Reviewer verdicts |
103	| `human-review` | Emergency stop: all agents call noop |
104	| `needs-rebase` | PR branch needs a merge from main; triggers conflict-resolver |
105	| `self-improvement`, `ci-fix`, `plan-file` | Provenance on factory-generated PRs |
106	| `workflow-health` | Tracking issues for data-layer failures |
107	| `automation`, `low-risk` | Applied to routine factory PRs |
108	| `pr-fix` | Applied to commits pushed by `/pr-fix` |
109	
110	Without these labels, workflows that try to `add-labels: allowed: [...]` will fail their safe-output validation.
111	
112	### Installed GitHub Apps
113	
114	- **GitHub Copilot** (coding agent + code review) - required for `impl:copilot` routing and inline review annotations
115	- **`githubnext/agentics`** workflows - installed via `gh aw add githubnext/agentics/<name>` (pulls `/pr-fix`, `issue-triage`)
116	
117	### First-run checklist
118	
119	- [ ] All local tooling installed and `gh auth status` clean
120	- [ ] Repository settings applied (workflow permissions, approval, Copilot)
121	- [ ] All required secrets present in Actions secrets (not environment or Dependabot)
122	- [ ] All required labels created
123	- [ ] `gh aw compile` run once locally so every `.md` workflow has a matching `.lock.yml`
124	- [ ] Test issue opened and labeled `needs-spec` to verify `spec-refiner` fires
125	
126	
127	## Quick Start: Your First Run
128

content.text:
Agreed. Pausing code and stepping back.

### Honest diagnosis of the board

The 6-column model inherits factory label noise it can't cleanly resolve. Symptoms we've already hit today:

1. **Open PRs without factory labels default to Inbox** — wrong semantically ("this item needs you to merge it" vs "this hasn't been started"). Fix in-flight (#166 pending).
2. **Items get overwritten by auto-add** — GitHub's "Item added to project" workflow sets Status=Inbox by default, racing with my sync.
3. **#161 closing bug** — spec-refiner wrote `Fixes #161`, auto-closed the issue on plan-merge. Not a board bug per se, but the board couldn't distinguish "done" from "prematurely killed."
4. **Label proliferation** — every new factory nuance (`needs-rebase`, `self-improvement`, `ai-reviewed`, `fast-track`, etc.) needs a re-ask of "which column does this go in?" Today it's 6 rules in bash; tomorrow it'll be 10.

All of it is symptom of one root problem: **the board is trying to render a 15-label state machine onto 6 columns, and the mapping is fragile.**

### Proposal: collapse to 3 or 4 columns

One operator, one repo. What actually matters at a glance:

**Option A — 3 columns, brutalist clarity**

| Column | Meaning | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| 🤖 **Factory working** | Agents have it, wait | Any `needs-spec`, `needs-plan`, `ready-for-implementation`, `assigned-to-agent` on open issue/PR |
| 👉 **Your turn** | You need to do something | Any open PR OR any open issue with `needs-changes`, `needs-rebase`, `human-review`, `blocked-on-human`, `ai-reviewed`, `plan-file` |
| ✅ **Done** | Closed or merged | `state=closed` |

**Option B — 4 columns, one extra for "not yet engaged"**

Same as A, but split `Factory working` into `📥 Waiting for spec` (just filed, no factory label yet or only `needs-spec`) and `🤖 Factory building` (has `ready-for-implementation` / `assigned-to-agent`).

### Why this is better

- **Every new label defaults to a sensible column.** Unknown label on an open PR? → Your turn (you're the fallback reviewer). Unknown label on an open issue? → Factory working (let it cook). No more "which column does this go in" edge cases.
- **No race with auto-add.** Auto-add sets Status to first option. Make that first option = Factory working. New items without labels go there, which is *correct* — nothing has happened yet, let the factory pick it up.
- **Fewer columns = fewer bugs.** 3 rules in the sync instead of 6.

### Bigger question: is the board even the right abstraction?

Alternative: **replace the board with two saved searches**:
- `Your turn`: `is:open (label:ai-reviewed OR label:plan-file OR label:needs-changes OR label:needs-rebase OR label:human-review OR label:blocked-on-human) OR (is:pr is:open -label:assigned-to-agent)`
- `Factory working`: `is:open label:assigned-to-agent OR label:needs-spec OR label:needs-plan OR label:ready-for-implementation`

Bookmark both. No Projects API, no sync workflow, no auto-add race, no column-mapping code.

### My vote

**Option A + keep the board** — the at-a-glance kanban is still useful for grouping visually, but with 3 columns it's simple enough to actually stay aligned. Close PRs #166 and #167 without merging (they fix symptoms of the 6-column model that go away under A). Delete the agent-activity-tracker workflow (#165) — marginal value now that the factory is 1-operator-low-volume.

### What I need from you

Pick A, B, or saved-searches-only. Or tell me the rethink should go deeper (different model entirely).

Don't pick based on my vote — pick based on what you'll actually check daily. The board is for *you*.

          IS_PR=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.pr')

          echo "Item: $REPO#$ISSUE_NUMBER  state=$ITEM_STATE  pr=$IS_PR  merged=$EVENT_MERGED"
          echo "Labels: $LABELS"

          # Priority-ordered label-to-lane derivation (4-column overview).
          # Rules, from highest priority:
          #  1) closed -> Done
          #  2) any human-action label, OR any open PR -> Your turn
          #  3) factory-progress labels (ready-for-implementation, assigned-to-agent, needs-plan) -> Factory building
          #  4) fallback -> Waiting for spec
          L=",$LABELS,"
          if [ "$ITEM_STATE" = "closed" ]; then
            STATE_NAME=Done
          elif [[ "$L" == *",needs-changes,"* \
               || "$L" == *",needs-rebase,"* \
               || "$L" == *",human-review,"* \
               || "$L" == *",blocked-on-human,"* \
               || "$L" == *",ai-reviewed,"* \
               || "$L" == *",plan-file,"* ]]; then
            STATE_NAME=YourTurn
          elif [ "$IS_PR" = "true" ] && [ "$ITEM_STATE" = "open" ]; then
            # Any open PR defaults to Your turn — you're the one who merges it.
            STATE_NAME=YourTurn
          elif [[ "$L" == *",ready-for-implementation,"* \
               || "$L" == *",assigned-to-agent,"* \
               || "$L" == *",needs-plan,"* ]]; then
            STATE_NAME=Factory
          else
            # needs-spec, no labels yet, or anything else the factory hasn't picked up.
            STATE_NAME=Waiting
          fi
          OPT_ID="${OPT[$STATE_NAME]}"
          echo "Lane -> $STATE_NAME ($OPT_ID)"

          # Ensure item is on the project (idempotent) + capture item id
          ITEM_ID=$(gh api graphql -f query='
            mutation($projectId: ID!, $contentId: ID!) {
              addProjectV2ItemById(input: { projectId: $projectId, contentId: $contentId }) {
                item { id }
              }
            }' -f projectId="$PROJECT_ID" -f contentId="$NODE_ID" \
            --jq '.data.addProjectV2ItemById.item.id')
          echo "Project item id: $ITEM_ID"

          # Update the Factory state field
          gh api graphql -f query='
            mutation($projectId: ID!, $itemId: ID!, $fieldId: ID!, $optId: String!) {
              updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue(input: {
                projectId: $projectId,
                itemId: $itemId,
                fieldId: $fieldId,
                value: { singleSelectOptionId: $optId }
              }) { projectV2Item { id } }
            }' -f projectId="$PROJECT_ID" -f itemId="$ITEM_ID" -f fieldId="$FIELD_ID" -f optId="$OPT_ID" \
            --jq '.data.updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue.projectV2Item.id'

          # Apply/remove the "your-turn" label so cards in Planning, Review,
          # or Needs Attention lanes show a visible chip wherever they appear.
          # Uses PROJECTS_PAT (which has `repo` scope) rather than GITHUB_TOKEN
          # because this workflow currently runs with `contents: read` only.
          case "$STATE_NAME" in
            Planning|Review|NeedsAttention)
              gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --add-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                || gh pr edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --add-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                || true
              ;;
            *)
              gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --remove-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                || gh pr edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --remove-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                || true
              ;;
          esac

### ✅ What's working end-to-end

| Stage | Reliability today |
|---|---|
| Issue labeled `needs-spec` → spec-refiner fires | ✓ |
| Spec-refiner opens plan PR | ✓ |
| Plan PR merged → `plan-merged-dispatcher` activates source issue | ✓ (uses `GH_AW_AGENT_TOKEN`, cascade fires) |

| Implementer-dispatcher assigns Copilot → Copilot opens impl PR | ✓ (#172 proof) |
| Impl PR → reviewer + contribution-checker + simplify-and-harden + eval-creator | ✓ (proven on #166, #167) |
| Board auto-add + label-driven Status sync | ✓ (4-column, clean) |

### ❌ Known broken / tracked as issues

| Gap | Status |
|---|---|
| Spec-refiner writes `Fixes #NN` → auto-closes source issue on plan merge | Tracked in **#171**, plan PR #173 open |
| Spec-refiner noop path leaves issues stuck | Tracked in **#169**, plan PR #170 open |
| #161 keeps re-closing (unknown cause, PAT-authored) | Not tracked; low priority since impl PR #172 exists |

- Sub-issue merge-conflict class: **gone** (#138)
- Silent skips of review workflows on Copilot PRs: **gone** (#145)
- Missing observability transcripts: **shipping** (#146)

### Verdict

**Yes, we're materially closer.** The chain from `needs-spec` all the way to impl PR is reliably automated *given spec-refiner doesn't inject a closing keyword*. The two remaining tracked factory bugs (#169, #171) are both in Your turn column as plan PRs, about to close themselves through the very chain they're fixing — that's the canonical proof.

After #172 merges, the next proof point is whether #170 and #173 cascade end-to-end clean. I'll be watching.

Add this to your `.claude/settings.json`:

```json

content.text:
Found it. gh-aw has **two concurrency layers** in `contribution-checker`:

```yaml
concurrency:                                               # top-level: per-PR, parallel
  group: "gh-aw-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}"
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  conclusion:                                              # job-level: singleton across repo
    concurrency:
      group: "gh-aw-conclusion-contribution-checker"
      cancel-in-progress: false
```

The top-level group is per-PR (different PRs run in parallel). But the final `conclusion` step is a **global singleton** — only one contribution-checker conclusion can execute at a time across the whole repo. Second PR's conclusion queues behind first.

That's why #173 looked "waiting" — #170's conclusion step was holding the lock. As soon as #170's conclusion finishes, #173's starts. The wait is intentional and typical for gh-aw workflows with safe-outputs (it prevents race conditions when two workflows try to label/comment simultaneously).

Same pattern applies to reviewer, simplify-and-harden, eval-creator — they all singleton-serialize their conclusion step. If you open N PRs at once, their reviews finish serially, not in parallel.

content.text:
Agreed. It's gh-aw's default, baked into every compiled `.lock.yml`. The design trades throughput for safety — singleton conclusion prevents race conditions when two workflows try to label/comment the same PR simultaneously.

For a 1-5 PR/day factory, cost is real but bounded: ~30s–2min extra latency per queued PR. For a busier repo it'd bite harder.

**If/when it becomes painful**, three paths:
1. Override per-workflow by hand-patching `.lock.yml` (fights the lock-sync CI guard — avoid).
2. Ask gh-aw for a frontmatter knob to narrow the conclusion concurrency (e.g. `conclusion-concurrency: per-pr`). Cleanest path; probably a 10-line upstream contribution.
3. Write a custom `gh aw compile` post-processor that rewrites the conclusion group key. Fragile.

Not a blocker today. Worth filing with gh-aw as a future contribution, not worth spending time on now.

      - `file-check`: verify file or section exists
      - `rule-check`: read target file, search for expected content

# Spec Refiner

You are the front door of the agent factory. An issue has been labeled `needs-spec`. Your job is to turn it into a structured plan file that downstream agents can execute against.

## Your skill

Read `.claude/skills/plan-interview/SKILL.md` in full and follow its process. That file is your source of truth for how to run the interview, explore the codebase, and structure the plan file output.

This is a single-shot gh-aw run, not a live session. Follow the skill's process, but when it expects to ask the user questions, apply rule 1 from the "Adapting skills for single-shot gh-aw runs" section of `AGENTS.md`: simulate the interview by answering from issue context, and mark anything you cannot answer with confidence using `**NEEDS HUMAN INPUT**` plus a specific question.

## Implementer recommendation

Before writing the PR, append a `## Recommended implementer` section to the plan file.

Always recommend `copilot`. Copilot is the only implementer the factory can auto-assign today. GitHub Partner Agents (Claude, Codex) are visible in the UI assignees picker but the REST API endpoint silently drops them, so `assign-to-user` cannot route to them from a workflow. Until GitHub exposes proper API assignment for Partner Agents, the `impl:claude-*` and `impl:codex` labels exist only as human-override signals for manual UI assignment.

Example:

```markdown
## Recommended implementer

**Choice**: copilot
**Rationale**: Auto-assignable via `implementer-dispatcher`. For manual hand-off to Claude or Codex (UI assignment only, no auto-dispatch), a human can swap the label on the source issue before merging the plan PR.
```

After writing the recommendation in the plan file, add the `impl:copilot` label to the source issue. A human can swap it to `impl:claude-opus`, `impl:claude-sonnet`, or `impl:codex` before merging if they want to hand-assign via the GitHub UI outside the factory.

## gh-aw handoff logic

After the skill completes, the plan file is written, and the implementer is recommended:

1. **Open a PR** with the new plan file at `docs/plans/plan-NNN-<slug>.md` where NNN is the source issue number, zero-padded to at least three digits (e.g., issue #7 → `007`, issue #42 → `042`, issue #1234 → `1234`). Do not scan `docs/plans/` for the next sequential number. Title: `[plan] Plan NNN: <title>` using the same padded issue number. Body references the source issue with `Refs #NN` (not a closing keyword such as `Closes` or `Fixes`). The plan PR must not close the source issue on merge. The body also summarizes the key decisions and restates the implementer recommendation.
2. **Comment on the source issue** with a one-line summary, a link to the plan PR, and the recommended implementer.
3. **Swap labels**:
   - Remove `needs-spec`
   - Add `impl:copilot`
   - Add `needs-plan` if the plan has no open questions. On merge of the plan PR, `plan-merged-dispatcher` reads the plan checklist, writes it onto the source issue body, and transitions `needs-plan` → `ready-for-implementation` on the source issue.
   - Add `blocked-on-human` if the plan has any `**NEEDS HUMAN INPUT**` markers

## Skip conditions (call noop)

Skip plan creation and call `noop` with a brief explanation comment when:
- The issue already has a linked plan file
- The issue is labeled `human-review`
- The skill's own criteria say this is not a plan-worthy task (simple bug fix, docs change, dependency bump, pure research)
- The issue is spam or unclear beyond recovery

## Style

Follow the writing rules in `AGENTS.md`. No em-dashes. Lead with the answer. Short declarative sentences.

## Session capture

This workflow's full session is automatically captured in the `agent` artifact for this run. The artifact includes the prompt, all tool calls, tool outputs, and token usage. The `learning-aggregator-ci` workflow downloads and analyzes these artifacts weekly to extract improvement patterns for the outer learning loop.

name: Plan Merged Dispatcher

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]
    paths:
      - 'docs/plans/plan-*.md'

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  dispatch:
    if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout merged plan file
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.merge_commit_sha }}
          sparse-checkout: docs/plans
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Activate source issues from merged plan files
        env:
          # Must be a PAT, not the default GITHUB_TOKEN. Events produced by
          # GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger downstream workflows (GitHub's
          # anti-loop rule), which would leave `implementer-dispatcher`
          # inert on the `ready-for-implementation` label we add below.
          # Uses GH_AW_AGENT_TOKEN because it already exists as a
          # configured secret in this repo (GH_AW_CI_TRIGGER_TOKEN was
          # referenced by an earlier fix but never existed) and is
          # scoped for issue editing + label-event cascades.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_AW_AGENT_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          PLAN_FILES=$(gh pr diff "$PR_NUMBER" --name-only \
            | grep -E '^docs/plans/plan-[0-9]+-.+\.md$' || true)

          if [ -z "$PLAN_FILES" ]; then
            echo "No plan files in this PR. Nothing to activate."
            exit 0
          fi

          activated=0
          while IFS= read -r plan_path; do
            [ -f "$plan_path" ] || { echo "Plan file missing after checkout: $plan_path"; continue; }

            filename=$(basename "$plan_path")
            issue_num=$(printf '%s' "$filename" | sed -E 's/^plan-0*([0-9]+)-.*\.md$/\1/')
            if ! [[ "$issue_num" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
              echo "Could not parse issue number from $filename; skipping."
              continue
            fi

            if ! gh issue view "$issue_num" --json state >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Issue #$issue_num not found; skipping $filename."
              continue
            fi

            checklist=$(awk '
              /^## Implementation Checklist[[:space:]]*$/ { grab=1; next }
              grab && /^## / { exit }
              grab { print }
            ' "$plan_path")

            if [ -z "$(printf '%s' "$checklist" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
              echo "Plan $filename has no Implementation Checklist section; skipping."
              continue
            fi

            plan_slug="${filename%.md}"
            marker_begin="<!-- plan-checklist:${plan_slug}:begin -->"
            marker_end="<!-- plan-checklist:${plan_slug}:end -->"

            current_body=$(gh issue view "$issue_num" --json body --jq .body)

            cleaned_body=$(printf '%s' "$current_body" \
              | awk -v begin="$marker_begin" -v end="$marker_end" '
                  index($0, begin) { skip=1; next }
                  skip && index($0, end) { skip=0; next }
                  !skip { print }
                ')

            cleaned_body=$(printf '%s' "$cleaned_body" | awk '
              /^[[:space:]]*$/ { blank++; next }
              { for (i=0;i<blank;i++) print ""; blank=0; print }
            ')

            {
              printf '%s\n' "$cleaned_body"
              printf '\n%s\n' "$marker_begin"
              printf '## Implementation Checklist (from %s)\n\n' "$plan_slug"
              printf '%s\n' "$checklist"
              printf '%s\n' "$marker_end"
            } > /tmp/issue_body.md

            gh issue edit "$issue_num" --body-file /tmp/issue_body.md
            gh issue edit "$issue_num" --remove-label needs-plan 2>/dev/null || true
            gh issue edit "$issue_num" --remove-label needs-spec 2>/dev/null || true
            gh issue edit "$issue_num" --add-label ready-for-implementation

            echo "Activated issue #$issue_num from $filename."
            activated=$((activated + 1))
          done <<< "$PLAN_FILES"

          echo "Activated $activated source issue(s)."

## Summary

Direct PR for #171 — the factory bug where spec-refiner kept writing `Fixes #NN` in plan PR bodies, causing GitHub to auto-close the source issue on plan-PR merge. Bypassing the factory because shipping it *through* the factory would have hit the same bug on the plan PR merge.

Two layers of fix:

### 1. Spec-refiner prompt hardening

Escalate the closing-keyword rule from one parenthetical aside to a standalone CRITICAL block. Explicit list of every forbidden variant (`Closes/Close/Closed/Fixes/Fix/Fixed/Resolves/Resolve/Resolved`), a regex self-check the model runs against its own draft, and safe synonyms to use instead (`Refs`, `For`, `Part of`, `Tracks`, `See`).

### 2. plan-merged-dispatcher defensive reopen

If the dispatcher fires on a plan-PR merge and finds the source issue `CLOSED`, reopen it with a comment explaining the bug. Survives any future spec-refiner regression — the factory self-corrects instead of silently dying.

## Evidence this is needed

Today alone, **three** source issues got auto-closed by this bug:

- #161 — plan PR #164 had `Fixes #161`, closed on merge, manual reopen
- #169 — plan PR #170 had `Fixes #169`, closed on merge, manual reopen
- #171 — plan PR #173 had `Fixes #171`, closed on merge (the very issue this PR fixes), manual reopen

Each required a human to reopen + re-toggle `ready-for-implementation` to get Copilot moving again. Defense-in-depth removes that toil.

- [ ] Confirm the reopen-on-close path fires if a future plan PR slips through with a closing keyword (manual test: temporarily add `Fixes #X` to a plan PR body, merge, watch plan-merged-dispatcher reopen #X)
- [ ] Next spec-refiner run on a new `needs-spec` issue: confirm the plan PR body does NOT contain any closing keywords

    Two-layer fix for the bug where spec-refiner kept writing `Fixes #NN`
    in plan PR bodies, auto-closing the source issue on plan-PR merge:

       parenthetical aside to a standalone CRITICAL block with every
       forbidden variant enumerated, a regex self-check, and explicit
       safe synonyms.
    2. plan-merged-dispatcher: if the source issue is CLOSED when the
       dispatcher fires, reopen it with a comment pointing at the bug.
       Defensive — survives any future spec-refiner regression.
    
    Closes #171
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

+++ b/.github/workflows/plan-merged-dispatcher.yml
@@ -99,6 +99,18 @@ jobs:
               printf '%s\n' "$marker_end"

+            fi

name: Sync Factory State

# Mirrors the factory label set onto the "AI Agent Factory" Projects v2 board's
# "Factory state" single-select field. Labels are authoritative; this workflow
# derives the projected state one-way. Never reads field -> back to labels.
#
# Requires a repo secret PROJECTS_PAT with `project` scope (fine-grained PAT,
# access to pskoett/measuring-ai-proficiency + project permission read/write).
# GITHUB_TOKEN cannot be used: Projects v2 requires a user PAT.

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled, unlabeled, closed, reopened, transferred]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, unlabeled, closed, reopened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: "Issue or PR number to resync (for manual testing)"
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: sync-factory-state-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Compute Factory state and update project item
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PROJECTS_PAT }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.issue_number }}
          EVENT_MERGED: ${{ github.event.pull_request.merged || 'false' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          PROJECT_ID='PVT_kwHOCpF41s4BU8ja'
          FIELD_ID='REDACTED'  # Status (4-column overview)

          # 4 lanes: Waiting for spec / Factory building / Your turn / Done.
          declare -A OPT=(
            [Waiting]='f75ad846'        # 📥 Waiting for spec
            [Factory]='47fc9ee4'        # 🤖 Factory building
            [YourTurn]='37fdf3fc'       # 👉 Your turn
            [Done]='675bf0bb'           # ✅ Done
          )

          # Fetch current labels + node id + state from REST (works for both issues and PRs)
          ITEM_JSON=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE_NUMBER" \
            --jq '{labels: [.labels[].name], node_id: .node_id, state: .state, pr: (has("pull_request"))}')
          LABELS=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.labels | join(",")')
          NODE_ID=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.node_id')
          ITEM_STATE=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.state')
          IS_PR=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.pr')

          echo "Item: $REPO#$ISSUE_NUMBER  state=$ITEM_STATE  pr=$IS_PR  merged=$EVENT_MERGED"
          echo "Labels: $LABELS"

          # Priority-ordered label-to-lane derivation (4-column overview).
          # Rules, from highest priority:
          #  1) closed -> Done
          #  2) any human-action label, OR any open PR -> Your turn
          #  3) factory-progress labels (ready-for-implementation, assigned-to-agent, needs-plan) -> Factory building
          #  4) fallback -> Waiting for spec
          L=",$LABELS,"
          if [ "$ITEM_STATE" = "closed" ]; then
            STATE_NAME=Done
          elif [[ "$L" == *",needs-changes,"* \
               || "$L" == *",needs-rebase,"* \
               || "$L" == *",human-review,"* \
               || "$L" == *",blocked-on-human,"* \
               || "$L" == *",ai-reviewed,"* \
               || "$L" == *",plan-file,"* ]]; then
            STATE_NAME=YourTurn
          elif [ "$IS_PR" = "true" ] && [ "$ITEM_STATE" = "open" ]; then
            # Any open PR defaults to Your turn — you're the one who merges it.
            STATE_NAME=YourTurn
          elif [[ "$L" == *",ready-for-implementation,"* \
               || "$L" == *",assigned-to-agent,"* \
               || "$L" == *",needs-plan,"* ]]; then
            STATE_NAME=Factory
          else
            # needs-spec, no labels yet, or anything else the factory hasn't picked up.
            STATE_NAME=Waiting
          fi
          OPT_ID="${OPT[$STATE_NAME]}"
          echo "Lane -> $STATE_NAME ($OPT_ID)"

          # Ensure item is on the project (idempotent) + capture item id
          ITEM_ID=$(gh api graphql -f query='
            mutation($projectId: ID!, $contentId: ID!) {
              addProjectV2ItemById(input: { projectId: $projectId, contentId: $contentId }) {
                item { id }
              }
            }' -f projectId="$PROJECT_ID" -f contentId="$NODE_ID" \
            --jq '.data.addProjectV2ItemById.item.id')
          echo "Project item id: $ITEM_ID"

          # Update the Factory state field
          gh api graphql -f query='
            mutation($projectId: ID!, $itemId: ID!, $fieldId: ID!, $optId: String!) {
              updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue(input: {
                projectId: $projectId,
                itemId: $itemId,
                fieldId: $fieldId,
                value: { singleSelectOptionId: $optId }
              }) { projectV2Item { id } }
            }' -f projectId="$PROJECT_ID" -f itemId="$ITEM_ID" -f fieldId="$FIELD_ID" -f optId="$OPT_ID" \
            --jq '.data.updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue.projectV2Item.id'

          # Apply/remove the "your-turn" label so cards in the Your turn lane
          # show a visible chip wherever they appear (Label view, filters, etc.).
          # Uses PROJECTS_PAT (which has `repo` scope) rather than GITHUB_TOKEN
          # because this workflow currently runs with `contents: read` only.
          case "$STATE_NAME" in
            YourTurn)
              gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --add-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                || gh pr edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --add-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                || true
              ;;
            *)
              gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --remove-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                || gh pr edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --remove-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                || true
              ;;
          esac

name: Sync Factory State

# Mirrors the factory label set onto the "AI Agent Factory" Projects v2 board's
# "Factory state" single-select field. Labels are authoritative; this workflow
# derives the projected state one-way. Never reads field -> back to labels.
#
# Requires a repo secret PROJECTS_PAT with `project` scope (fine-grained PAT,
# access to pskoett/measuring-ai-proficiency + project permission read/write).
# GITHUB_TOKEN cannot be used: Projects v2 requires a user PAT.

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened, edited, labeled, unlabeled, closed, reopened, transferred]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, labeled, unlabeled, closed, reopened, ready_for_review, converted_to_draft]
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'  # reconcile open items every 10 min as a safety net
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: "Issue or PR number to resync (for manual testing)"
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: sync-factory-state-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Compute Factory state and update project item
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PROJECTS_PAT }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.issue_number }}
          EVENT_MERGED: ${{ github.event.pull_request.merged || 'false' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          PROJECT_ID='PVT_kwHOCpF41s4BU8ja'
          FIELD_ID='REDACTED'  # Status (4-column overview)

          # 4 lanes: Waiting for spec / Factory building / Your turn / Done.
          declare -A OPT=(
            [Waiting]='f75ad846'        # 📥 Waiting for spec
            [Factory]='47fc9ee4'        # 🤖 Factory building
            [YourTurn]='37fdf3fc'       # 👉 Your turn
            [Done]='675bf0bb'           # ✅ Done
          )

          # Fetch current labels + node id + state from REST (works for both issues and PRs)
          ITEM_JSON=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE_NUMBER" \
            --jq '{labels: [.labels[].name], node_id: .node_id, state: .state, pr: (has("pull_request"))}')
          LABELS=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.labels | join(",")')
          NODE_ID=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.node_id')
          ITEM_STATE=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.state')
          IS_PR=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.pr')

          echo "Item: $REPO#$ISSUE_NUMBER  state=$ITEM_STATE  pr=$IS_PR  merged=$EVENT_MERGED"
          echo "Labels: $LABELS"

          # Priority-ordered label-to-lane derivation (4-column overview).
          # Rules, from highest priority:
          #  1) closed -> Done
          #  2) any human-action label, OR any open PR -> Your turn
          #  3) factory-progress labels (ready-for-implementation, assigned-to-agent, needs-plan) -> Factory building
          #  4) fallback -> Waiting for spec
          L=",$LABELS,"
          if [ "$ITEM_STATE" = "closed" ]; then
            STATE_NAME=Done
          elif [[ "$L" == *",needs-changes,"* \
               || "$L" == *",needs-rebase,"* \
               || "$L" == *",human-review,"* \
               || "$L" == *",blocked-on-human,"* \
               || "$L" == *",ai-reviewed,"* \
               || "$L" == *",plan-file,"* ]]; then
            STATE_NAME=YourTurn
          elif [ "$IS_PR" = "true" ] && [ "$ITEM_STATE" = "open" ]; then
            # Any open PR defaults to Your turn — you're the one who merges it.
            STATE_NAME=YourTurn
          elif [[ "$L" == *",ready-for-implementation,"* \
               || "$L" == *",assigned-to-agent,"* \
               || "$L" == *",needs-plan,"* ]]; then
            STATE_NAME=Factory
          else
            # needs-spec, no labels yet, or anything else the factory hasn't picked up.
            STATE_NAME=Waiting
          fi
          OPT_ID="${OPT[$STATE_NAME]}"
          echo "Lane -> $STATE_NAME ($OPT_ID)"

          # Ensure item is on the project (idempotent) + capture item id
          ITEM_ID=$(gh api graphql -f query='
            mutation($projectId: ID!, $contentId: ID!) {
              addProjectV2ItemById(input: { projectId: $projectId, contentId: $contentId }) {
                item { id }
              }
            }' -f projectId="$PROJECT_ID" -f contentId="$NODE_ID" \
            --jq '.data.addProjectV2ItemById.item.id')
          echo "Project item id: $ITEM_ID"

          # Update the Factory state field
          gh api graphql -f query='
            mutation($projectId: ID!, $itemId: ID!, $fieldId: ID!, $optId: String!) {
              updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue(input: {
                projectId: $projectId,
                itemId: $itemId,
                fieldId: $fieldId,
                value: { singleSelectOptionId: $optId }
              }) { projectV2Item { id } }
            }' -f projectId="$PROJECT_ID" -f itemId="$ITEM_ID" -f fieldId="$FIELD_ID" -f optId="$OPT_ID" \
            --jq '.data.updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue.projectV2Item.id'

          # Apply/remove the "your-turn" label so cards in the Your turn lane
          # show a visible chip wherever they appear (Label view, filters, etc.).
          # Uses PROJECTS_PAT (which has `repo` scope) rather than GITHUB_TOKEN
          # because this workflow currently runs with `contents: read` only.
          case "$STATE_NAME" in
            YourTurn)
              gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --add-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                || gh pr edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --add-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                || true
              ;;
            *)
              gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --remove-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                || gh pr edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --remove-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                || true
              ;;
          esac

name: Sync Factory State

# Mirrors the factory label set onto the "AI Agent Factory" Projects v2 board's
# "Factory state" single-select field. Labels are authoritative; this workflow
# derives the projected state one-way. Never reads field -> back to labels.
#
# Requires a repo secret PROJECTS_PAT with `project` scope (fine-grained PAT,
# access to pskoett/measuring-ai-proficiency + project permission read/write).
# GITHUB_TOKEN cannot be used: Projects v2 requires a user PAT.

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened, edited, labeled, unlabeled, closed, reopened, transferred]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, labeled, unlabeled, closed, reopened, ready_for_review, converted_to_draft]
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'  # reconcile open items every 10 min as a safety net
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: "Issue or PR number to resync (for manual testing)"
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: sync-factory-state-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.issue_number || 'scheduled' }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Compute Factory state and update project item
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PROJECTS_PAT }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.issue_number }}
          EVENT_MERGED: ${{ github.event.pull_request.merged || 'false' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          PROJECT_ID='PVT_kwHOCpF41s4BU8ja'
          FIELD_ID='REDACTED'  # Status (4-column overview)

          # 4 lanes: Waiting for spec / Factory building / Your turn / Done.
          declare -A OPT=(
            [Waiting]='f75ad846'        # 📥 Waiting for spec
            [Factory]='47fc9ee4'        # 🤖 Factory building
            [YourTurn]='37fdf3fc'       # 👉 Your turn
            [Done]='675bf0bb'           # ✅ Done
          )

          # Scheduled / no-item runs reconcile every open issue + PR + the
          # handful of recently-closed items (so Done transitions are picked
          # up promptly). Single-item runs process just the triggering item.
          if [ -z "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" ]; then
            echo "No item number — reconciling all open issues and PRs + 10 most recently closed."
            ALL=$({ gh issue list --state all --limit 30 --json number --jq '.[].number'; \
                    gh pr list    --state all --limit 30 --json number --jq '.[].number'; } \
                    | sort -un)
            SELF=$(dirname "$0")
            for n in $ALL; do
              echo "::group::item #$n"
              ISSUE_NUMBER=$n "$0" "$@" || true
              echo "::endgroup::"
            done
            # The recursion above is fake — we just re-enter the processing
            # block. Simpler: handle the loop inline.
            for n in $ALL; do
              ISSUE_NUMBER=$n
              # fall through to per-item block by re-entering the function below
              process_item "$n" || true
            done
            exit 0
          fi

          # Fetch current labels + node id + state from REST (works for both issues and PRs)
          ITEM_JSON=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE_NUMBER" \
            --jq '{labels: [.labels[].name], node_id: .node_id, state: .state, pr: (has("pull_request"))}')
          LABELS=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.labels | join(",")')
          NODE_ID=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.node_id')
          ITEM_STATE=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.state')
          IS_PR=$(echo "$ITEM_JSON" | jq -r '.pr')

name: Sync Factory State

# Mirrors the factory label set onto the "AI Agent Factory" Projects v2 board's
# Status field. Labels are authoritative; this workflow derives the projected
# state one-way. Never reads field -> back to labels.
#
# Runs on:
#  - issue/PR state or label changes (per-item sync)
#  - scheduled cron every 10 min (reconcile all open items, catches missed events)
#  - workflow_dispatch (manual resync of a specific item)
#
# Requires a repo secret PROJECTS_PAT with `project` scope (fine-grained PAT,
# access to pskoett/measuring-ai-proficiency + project permission read/write).
# GITHUB_TOKEN cannot be used: Projects v2 requires a user PAT.

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened, edited, labeled, unlabeled, closed, reopened, transferred]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, labeled, unlabeled, closed, reopened, ready_for_review, converted_to_draft]
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'  # reconcile all open items every 10 min as a safety net
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: "Issue or PR number to resync (leave empty for full reconcile)"
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: sync-factory-state-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.issue_number || 'scheduled' }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Compute Factory state and update project item
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PROJECTS_PAT }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.issue_number }}
          EVENT_MERGED: ${{ github.event.pull_request.merged || 'false' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          PROJECT_ID='PVT_kwHOCpF41s4BU8ja'
          FIELD_ID='REDACTED'  # Status (4-column overview)

          # 4 lanes: Waiting for spec / Factory building / Your turn / Done.
          declare -A OPT=(
            [Waiting]='f75ad846'        # 📥 Waiting for spec
            [Factory]='47fc9ee4'        # 🤖 Factory building
            [YourTurn]='37fdf3fc'       # 👉 Your turn
            [Done]='675bf0bb'           # ✅ Done
          )

          sync_one() {
            local num="$1"

            local item_json labels node_id item_state is_pr
            item_json=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$num" \
              --jq '{labels: [.labels[].name], node_id: .node_id, state: .state, pr: (has("pull_request"))}' 2>/dev/null) || {
              echo "  skip #$num: not accessible"
              return 0
            }
            labels=$(echo "$item_json" | jq -r '.labels | join(",")')
            node_id=$(echo "$item_json" | jq -r '.node_id')
            item_state=$(echo "$item_json" | jq -r '.state')
            is_pr=$(echo "$item_json" | jq -r '.pr')

            local L=",$labels,"
            local state_name
            if [ "$item_state" = "closed" ]; then
              state_name=Done
            elif [[ "$L" == *",needs-changes,"* \
                 || "$L" == *",needs-rebase,"* \
                 || "$L" == *",human-review,"* \
                 || "$L" == *",blocked-on-human,"* \
                 || "$L" == *",ai-reviewed,"* \
                 || "$L" == *",plan-file,"* ]]; then
              state_name=YourTurn
            elif [ "$is_pr" = "true" ] && [ "$item_state" = "open" ]; then
              state_name=YourTurn
            elif [[ "$L" == *",ready-for-implementation,"* \
                 || "$L" == *",assigned-to-agent,"* \
                 || "$L" == *",needs-plan,"* ]]; then
              state_name=Factory
            else
              state_name=Waiting
            fi
            local opt_id="${OPT[$state_name]}"
            echo "  #$num state=$item_state pr=$is_pr labels=[$labels] -> $state_name"

            local item_id
            item_id=$(gh api graphql -f query='
              mutation($projectId: ID!, $contentId: ID!) {
                addProjectV2ItemById(input: { projectId: $projectId, contentId: $contentId }) {
                  item { id }
                }
              }' -f projectId="$PROJECT_ID" -f contentId="$node_id" \
              --jq '.data.addProjectV2ItemById.item.id' 2>/dev/null) || return 0

            gh api graphql -f query='
              mutation($projectId: ID!, $itemId: ID!, $fieldId: ID!, $optId: String!) {
                updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue(input: {
                  projectId: $projectId,
                  itemId: $itemId,
                  fieldId: $fieldId,
                  value: { singleSelectOptionId: $optId }
                }) { projectV2Item { id } }
              }' -f projectId="$PROJECT_ID" -f itemId="$item_id" -f fieldId="$FIELD_ID" -f optId="$opt_id" \
              --jq '.data.updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue.projectV2Item.id' >/dev/null || true

            case "$state_name" in
              YourTurn)
                gh issue edit "$num" --add-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                  || gh pr edit "$num" --add-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                  || true
                ;;
              *)
                gh issue edit "$num" --remove-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                  || gh pr edit "$num" --remove-label your-turn --repo "$REPO" 2>/dev/null \
                  || true
                ;;
            esac
          }

          if [ -z "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" ]; then
            echo "No item number — full reconcile of open items + 15 most recent closed."
            ITEMS=$({ gh issue list --state all --limit 30 --json number --jq '.[].number'; \
                      gh pr list    --state all --limit 30 --json number --jq '.[].number'; } \
                      | sort -un)
            for n in $ITEMS; do
              sync_one "$n" || true
            done
          else
            sync_one "$ISSUE_NUMBER"
          fi

**Spec-refiner's fast-track path (shipped in #175) doesn't cascade.** When it adds `ready-for-implementation` via its `add-labels` safe-output, the label event is attributed to `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which GitHub blocks from triggering downstream workflows (anti-loop rule).

input.content:
## Problem

`spec-refiner`'s fast-track path (added in #175) applies `ready-for-implementation` and `impl:copilot` directly when an issue is judged "not plan-worthy, can go to direct implementation." This is meant to route the issue straight to `implementer-dispatcher` without a plan PR.

But it doesn't work end-to-end. The labels are applied via gh-aw's `add-labels` safe-output, which uses `GITHUB_TOKEN`. GitHub's anti-loop rule blocks events attributed to `GITHUB_TOKEN` from triggering other workflows. Result: `implementer-dispatcher` never fires, Copilot never gets assigned, the issue sits with the right labels but no actual progress.
